referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 18 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 6 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 1 carries the modeled reference label: reference curve from a modeled expectation. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 12 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. 1 function rests on a method adopted from EASI's national screening method (provisional), because no reference pool, national donor, model, published benchmark or flagged transfer supported the function in this ecoregion. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. config.caveat: Specific conductance carries natural carbonate geology as well as disturbance: a pristine stream in a calcareous valley can score low on this curve.
config.notes: Specific conductance; higher indicates ionic disturbance (worse).
Total nitrogen; higher indicates nutrient enrichment (worse). The total fraction, reported in every NRSA cycle, and the fraction published nitrogen criteria are written against.
Total phosphorus; higher indicates nutrient enrichment (worse).
Turbidity; higher indicates more suspended sediment (worse).

NRSA fish multimetric index (0 to 100); higher is better. Eight metrics per NARS-9 region, several adjusted for watershed area, scored from an electrofishing sample; sites sampled by seining carry no index.
Percent of native fish individuals classed tolerant (TOLERANCE_NRSA); higher is worse. Dominance by tolerant fish is a standard multimetric-index component of disturbance.
Large woody debris volume per 100 m; higher is better.

config.caveat: pH carries natural geology (calcareous or naturally acidic waters) as well as disturbance, and a two-sided core narrower than measurement precision is noise rather than condition.
config.notes: pH degrades condition at BOTH extremes. Two-sided (optimum) curve: scored 1.0 across the reference interquartile core, falling in both tails.
Residual pool depth per 100 m; deeper residual pools generally better habitat.
